subject: SCIENCE
title: Heat and Electricity
objective: Identify safe everyday sources and uses through on-screen sorting only.
introduction: The Sun warms your skin, and a lamp lights the room. How do heat and electricity help us — and how do we stay safe?

vocabulary.definition: Energy that makes lights and machines work.
The power to do work, like light or heat.

items.prompt: Which statement about heat and electricity is true?

options.text: Heat is energy transfer related to temperature differences; electricity involves electric charge.

items.explanation: Heat moves from warmer to cooler things, and electricity is energy that flows. Poking outlets and touching hot pans are unsafe.

items.prompt: Which example shows a safe use of energy?

options.text: touch a hot pan with bare hands
insert a fork into an outlet

items.explanation: Sunlight warming a surface is a safe, everyday use of energy. Touching hot pans and poking outlets are dangerous.
Putting anything into an outlet can give a dangerous shock. Sunlight warming things and batteries powering safe devices are fine with adult care.

items.prompt: What should a child do about a damaged cord?

options.text: Tell a responsible adult and do not touch it.

items.explanation: A damaged cord can be dangerous, so tell an adult and do not touch it. Repairing it while plugged in or putting it in water is unsafe.
An adult can safely handle a damaged cord. Poking objects into outlets and short-circuiting batteries are dangerous.
